```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Quinney_2013_midazolam_ketoconazole_ddi_pbpk"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Quinney_2013_midazolam_ketoconazole_ddi_pbpk"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1038/psp.2013.50> (open access, PMC4026634)
* Structural model: Chien et al. 2006, <https://doi.org/10.1124/dmd.105.008730>

Quinney 2013 has two parts. The first re-analyses six published human liver
microsome studies of ketoconazole inhibiting midazolam 1'-hydroxylation,
fitting competitive (C), noncompetitive (NC) and mixed (M) inhibition models
combined with several microsomal-binding models (Table 3). Those fits are
algebraic Michaelis-Menten regressions on in vitro rates, not a dosing
model, so they are not packaged. Their output, the binding-corrected
inhibition constants, feeds the second part: a semi-physiological
midazolam / ketoconazole interaction model (Chien et al. 2006) that predicts
how much 200 mg ketoconazole daily raises the AUC of intravenous midazolam
under each inhibition mechanism (Figure 3, Table 4). That in vivo model is
what is packaged here, transcribed from the authors' R code in the
Supplementary Data.

```{r load-model}
mod <- readModelDb("Quinney_2013_midazolam_ketoconazole_ddi_pbpk")
mod_rx <- rxode2::rxode2(mod)
```

# Population

The paper simulates one typical subject with the mean parameters ("A single
subject was simulated for each inhibition type using the mean parameters").
The comparator data are from a healthy-volunteer study in which ketoconazole
200 mg was given once daily before intravenous midazolam (Quinney 2013
ref. 16, Lucksiri 2005, PhD thesis, Purdue University), with every
midazolam concentration normalised to a 1 mg dose. The model has no
covariates, no between-subject variability and no residual error.

# Source trace

Every value is transcribed from the parameter vector in
`PSP-2013-0039-s07.txt` (the authors' simulation script); the ODEs are the
three functions of `PSP-2013-0039-s06.txt`. The code labels the values it took
from Chien et al. 2006 with "Chien, 2006".

| Quantity | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Midazolam ka, kpv | 1.17, 1400 1/h | s07 para[1], para[2] |
| Midazolam V4 (central), V5 (peripheral), Q4 | 43 L, 88.4 L, 14.73 L/h | s07 para[3]-para[5] |
| Midazolam Vmax gut wall, Vmax liver | 2549, 2549 + 206 mg/h | s07 para[6], para[7] |
| Midazolam Km | 5.8 x 0.362 = 2.0996 mg/L | s07 para[8] |
| fm (CYP3A fraction of hepatic metabolism) | 0.93 | s07 para[18] |
| fu,MDZ, fu,KTZ | 0.04, 0.01 | s07 para[22], para[23]; Methods text below Eq. 9 |
| Midazolam renal clearance | 0.06 L/h | s07 para[33] |
| Ketoconazole ka, V51, V61, Q5 | 1.10 1/h, 32.1 L, 19.6 L, 2.39 L/h | s07 para[9]-para[11], para[14] |
| Ketoconazole Vmax, Km (liver) | 41.1 mg/h, 0.810 mg/L | s07 para[15], para[16] |
| Ketoconazole fukCL, fukEff | 1, 1 | s07 para[24], para[25] |
| Ketoconazole liver-to-enzyme-site k2e, Tmax, keff | 1 1/h, 1 mg/h, 5 mg/L | s07 para[13], para[34], para[12] |
| Vpv, Qpv, Qh | 0.07 L, 67.5 L/h, 90 L/h | s07 para[26]-para[28] |
| Vh (midazolam liver), Vhk (ketoconazole liver), Ve, Vgw | 1.5, 0.825, 0.825, 1 L | s07 para[29], para[30], para[35], para[32] |
| Kic, Kin (mixed, BIM) | 19.2, 39.8 nmol/L | Table 3 (BIM, M); s07 para[38], para[37] |
| Kic (competitive, BIM) | 4.2 nmol/L | Table 3 (BIM, C); s07 para[17] |
| Kin (noncompetitive, BIM) | 33.5 nmol/L | Table 3 (BIM, NC) |
| Ketoconazole MW for nmol/L to mg/L | 531.4 g/mol | s07 para[37], para[38] |
| Hepatic CLint, three inhibition forms | -- | Eqs. 9-11; s06 `competitive.model`, `noncompetitive.model`, `mixed.inhibition.model` |
| Midazolam and ketoconazole mass balances | -- | s06 (all three functions share them) |

The competitive and noncompetitive functions of s06 are the mixed function
with, respectively, the noncompetitive term removed (`kin` infinite) and
`kic = kin`. The packaged model is the mixed form; the other two are run below
by overriding `kic` and `kin`.

```{r inhibition-settings}
inhibition <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,       ~kic,  ~kin,
  "Competitive",     4.2,  1e12, # Table 3, BIM / C
  "Noncompetitive", 33.5,  33.5, # Table 3, BIM / NC
  "Mixed",          19.2,  39.8  # Table 3, BIM / M (the packaged values)
)
inhibition
```

# Simulation

Following the authors' script (s07): ketoconazole 200 mg orally once daily
at 0, 24, ..., 120 h (six doses), and midazolam 1 mg intravenously with the
sixth ketoconazole dose at 120 h. The control arm is midazolam 1 mg alone.
Observations are on the midazolam `central` state; `Cc` is returned in
ug/L.

```{r simulate}
obs_grid <- seq(0, 24, by = 0.1)

ev_alone <- rxode2::et(amt = 1, cmt = "central", time = 0) |>
  rxode2::et(time = obs_grid, cmt = "central") |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = 1L, treatment = "Midazolam alone")

ev_ddi <- rxode2::et(amt = 200, cmt = "depot_ketoconazole", time = 0, ii = 24, addl = 5) |>
  rxode2::et(amt = 1, cmt = "central", time = 120) |>
  rxode2::et(time = 120 + obs_grid, cmt = "central") |>
  as.data.frame()

sim_one <- function(events, kic, kin) {
  rxode2::rxSolve(
    mod_rx, events,
    params = c(kic = kic, kin = kin),
    atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-8,
    returnType = "data.frame"
  )
}

sim_alone <- sim_one(ev_alone, kic = 19.2, kin = 39.8) |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = "Midazolam alone", tad = time)

sim_ddi <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(inhibition)), function(i) {
  sim_one(ev_ddi, kic = inhibition$kic[i], kin = inhibition$kin[i]) |>
    dplyr::mutate(treatment = inhibition$treatment[i], tad = time - 120)
}))

sim <- dplyr::bind_rows(sim_alone, sim_ddi) |>
  dplyr::filter(tad >= 0) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    treatment = factor(
      treatment,
      levels = c("Midazolam alone", "Competitive", "Noncompetitive", "Mixed")
    )
  )
```

# Replicate published figures

## Figure 3a: midazolam alone

The authors' script simulates the control profile with a 3.5 mg intravenous
dose (s07: `ystart[5]=ystart[5]+3.5`), which is why Figure 3a starts near
80 ug/L (3.5 mg / 43 L) rather than near 23 ug/L.

```{r fig3a, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 3a of Quinney 2013: intravenous midazolam alone (3.5 mg, as in the authors' script)."}
sim_3a <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod_rx,
  rxode2::et(amt = 3.5, cmt = "central", time = 0) |>
    rxode2::et(time = obs_grid, cmt = "central"),
  returnType = "data.frame"
)
ggplot(sim_3a, aes(time, Cc)) +
  geom_line(colour = "blue") +
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(0.1, 100)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 8, 16, 24)) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Midazolam (ug/L)")
```

## Figure 3b: midazolam with ketoconazole, three inhibition models

```{r fig3b, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 3b of Quinney 2013: midazolam 1 mg IV with the sixth daily 200 mg ketoconazole dose. Blue competitive, red mixed, green noncompetitive, as in the paper."}
sim |>
  dplyr::filter(treatment != "Midazolam alone") |>
  ggplot(aes(tad, Cc, colour = treatment)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Competitive = "blue", Mixed = "red", Noncompetitive = "darkgreen")) +
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(0.1, 100)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 8, 16, 24)) +
  labs(x = "Time after midazolam dose (h)", y = "Midazolam (ug/L)", colour = NULL)
```

The ordering and spacing of the three curves match Figure 3b: the
competitive model (Kic 4.2 nmol/L) gives the most inhibition, the
noncompetitive model the least, and the mixed model lies between them, close
to the observed profiles.

# PKNCA validation

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::transmute(id = as.integer(treatment), time = tad, Cc, treatment)

dose_df <- sim_nca |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, treatment) |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = 0, amt = 1)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id, route = "intravascular")

intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0,
  end = Inf,
  cmax = TRUE,
  auclast = TRUE,
  aucinf.obs = TRUE,
  half.life = TRUE
)

nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
summary(nca_res)
```

## Comparison against published values

Results reports the predicted midazolam AUC without inhibitor as 0.031
against an observed 0.032, printed with units "ng/ml/h". A 1 mg intravenous
dose cleared at about 30 L/h gives an AUC near 0.03 mg h/L, so the printed
value is read as 0.031 mg h/L = 31 ug h/L. The paper does not say how its
AUCs were computed; AUC0-inf is used here.

```{r nca-compare}
reference <- tibble::tibble(treatment = "Midazolam alone", aucinf.obs = 31)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = reference,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(aucinf.obs = "ug*h/L"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated vs. the paper's predicted midazolam AUC without inhibitor.")
```

The AUC ratios (AUCR) of Table 4 are computed from the same PKNCA results.

```{r aucr}
auc_tbl <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("auclast", "aucinf.obs")) |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)

ctrl <- auc_tbl |> dplyr::filter(treatment == "Midazolam alone")

aucr <- auc_tbl |>
  dplyr::filter(treatment != "Midazolam alone") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    aucr_0_24 = auclast / ctrl$auclast,
    aucr_inf = aucinf.obs / ctrl$aucinf.obs,
    treatment = as.character(treatment)
  ) |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    tibble::tibble(
      treatment = c("Competitive", "Noncompetitive", "Mixed"),
      paper = c(4.5, 2.0, 2.5)
    ),
    by = "treatment"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (aucr_inf - paper) / paper)

aucr |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, aucr_0_24, aucr_inf, paper, pct_diff) |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(c(aucr_0_24, aucr_inf, pct_diff), \(x) signif(x, 3))) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Inhibition model" = treatment,
    "Simulated AUCR (0-24 h)" = aucr_0_24,
    "Simulated AUCR (0-inf)" = aucr_inf,
    "Table 4 AUCR" = paper,
    "Difference, 0-inf (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Midazolam AUC ratio with / without ketoconazole. Observed (Table 4): 3.1 (2.8-3.3).")
```

```{r gate}
# Deterministic model: one typical subject per arm, no random effects, so
# the differences below are transcription / method differences only.
ctrl_auc <- ctrl$aucinf.obs
stopifnot(
  abs(ctrl_auc - 31) / 31 < 0.10,
  all(abs(aucr$pct_diff) < 10),
  aucr$aucr_inf[aucr$treatment == "Competitive"] >
    aucr$aucr_inf[aucr$treatment == "Mixed"],
  aucr$aucr_inf[aucr$treatment == "Mixed"] >
    aucr$aucr_inf[aucr$treatment == "Noncompetitive"]
)
```

All three predicted AUCRs are within 10% of Table 4 and the mixed model is
the closest to the observed 3.1, as the paper concludes. AUC0-inf reproduces
Table 4 better than AUC0-24 does, which suggests the paper's AUCs were
extrapolated to infinity.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Source of the equations and constants.** The text defers to Chien et al.
  2006 for "all other equations and parameters". The authors' R code
  (Supplementary Data s06 and s07) contains the complete ODE system and every
  constant, so the model is transcribed from the code; Chien et al. 2006 was
  not needed.
- **Unbound fraction in the CLint equations.** Printed Eqs. 9-11 multiply Km
  by fu,MDZ in the denominator, which makes fu,MDZ cancel. The code applies
  fu,MDZ to the substrate term only (`km * Vh * (...) + fum * Ah * (...)`),
  so Km acts on unbound midazolam. The code's form is used.
- **Midazolam Km.** Methods says the simulation used the Km from the BIM
  binding model (3.30-3.48 umol/L, Table 3). The code uses 5.8 umol/L x 0.362
  = 2.10 mg/L, the value it labels "Chien, 2006". The code's value is used;
  it reproduces the paper's predicted control AUC (0.031 mg h/L).
- **Inhibition constants per model.** The example script (s07) runs the
  noncompetitive model with Kin = 39.8 nmol/L, the mixed-model value. Methods
  says each model used its own BIM constants, and with the noncompetitive
  BIM value of Table 3 (Kin = 33.5 nmol/L) the AUCR is closer to Table 4
  (2.0); 33.5 nmol/L is used for the noncompetitive arm here. The competitive
  arm uses Kic = 4.2 nmol/L (Table 3, BIM / C, and s07 para[17]).
- **Ketoconazole regimen.** Results states ketoconazole was given for 7 days
  in one place and 6 days in another; the script gives six once-daily doses
  with midazolam at the sixth, which is what is simulated.
- **Figure 3a dose.** Figure 3a is simulated at 3.5 mg, the dose in the
  authors' control script, although Results says concentrations were
  normalised to 1 mg. The AUC and AUCR comparisons use 1 mg.
- **Route flags and dummy state.** The code multiplies the oral-midazolam
  equations by a flag `modose` (0 in the paper's simulation) and keeps a
  ketoconazole portal-vein state whose derivative is identically zero. Here
  the route is chosen by the compartment that is dosed (`depot` for oral,
  `central` for intravenous midazolam) and the zero state is omitted. The
  paper only simulated intravenous midazolam, so the oral path, including
  gut-wall inhibition by ketoconazole still in the gut lumen, is shipped as
  coded but was not evaluated by the authors.
- **Zero-order infusion term.** The code carries an infusion rate `Dinf`
  (0 in every run) in both central compartments. It is omitted; an infusion
  into `central` is given with an rxode2 `rate` instead.
- **No variability.** The paper reports no between-subject or residual
  variability for the in vivo model, so none is included.
- Europe PMC, which carries PubMed's comment and correction links, lists no
  erratum or correction for this article as of 2026-11-23.
